description: Production Browser Driver DOM capture against a controlled public-shaped origin in an egress-less Docker network; every item launches the configured real Chrome broker path.

BF0.fault: kill the separate Artifact provider after the real Chrome document request starts

BF1.fault: kill both the Chrome execution daemon and separate Artifact provider after the document request starts

BF2.fault: kill Atoll Server after the real Chrome document request starts while keeping the execution daemon alive

BF3.fault: pause the isolated MySQL container after the real Chrome document request starts while keeping Atoll Server and the execution daemon alive

correctness_gates: the production Browser Driver and real Chrome reach the isolated public-shaped address without a private-network bypass
the controlled origin has no external network route and publishes an allowing robots policy
a normal user previews and confirms the exact immutable live_refetch Backfill
every job receives exactly one document request and every successful Attempt writes one bounded DOM response Artifact, trace Artifact, and BackfillOutput
all DOM Resource hashes match MySQL metadata and contain the expected extracted job identity
all effect attestations allow only GET or HEAD, same-origin documents, no forms, downloads, popups, or writes
all domain event intents reach the Channel ledger and restart preserves state, replay, presence, and Resource reads
fault_correctness_gates: BF0 uses a real Chrome process on the execution daemon and a separately authenticated Artifact provider daemon
the provider is killed only after the Browser Attempt is running and the controlled origin has accepted the document request
the old Attempt expires without an accepted Artifact or business result and its originating dispatch is durably settled
provider recovery allows a fresh dispatch and distinct Attempt to persist one DOM response, one effect trace and one BackfillOutput
all Permits and execution dispatches settle, and Server restart preserves provider presence and both Resource reads
BF1 additionally requires the control Actor to expire the old Attempt while both execution-side daemons are absent, then deliver recovery only after both devices reconnect
BF2 requires the same daemon process to survive the carrier outage, reconnect with a new Executor incarnation, fence the pre-outage Attempt, and complete with a fresh Attempt
BF3 pauses MySQL only after the Browser Attempt is running, the origin has accepted exactly one document request, and no Artifact exists

BF3 requires Atoll Server and the execution daemon to remain alive, then the original Attempt must commit exactly one DOM, one trace, and one BackfillOutput after MySQL resumes without a recovery dispatch or website refetch
non_claims: the controlled origin does not represent third-party JavaScript complexity, latency, rate limits, bot defenses, authentication, or site availability
B0/B1/B2 do not substitute for an authorized third-party canary, production egress isolation, or long-window SLO
Browser tasks remain on the single-item execution protocol until independent batch safety is demonstrated
BF3 demonstrates a bounded local database stall and connection resumption, not MySQL failover, connection reset, a remote database, or a Server/MySQL joint outage
